title: Additivity descends through an additive localization
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be additive categories [def-weil-additive-category]. Let $W$ be a class of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ and let $q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive localization at $W$ [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor, lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Assume explicitly that every object of $\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to some $qX$. Let $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ be additive, let $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be a functor and let $e:G\circ q\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ be a natural isomorphism. Then $G$ is additive. No calculus of fractions for $W$ is assumed.
